source.title: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets
source.authors: Adam Zaremba; Mehmet Huseyin Bilgin; Huaigang Long; Aleksander Mercik; Jan J. Szczygielski

hypothesis: The sign of one-day return persistence depends on liquidity: the most liquid coins exhibit daily momentum while the less liquid majority exhibit daily reversal.
mechanism: The source attributes broad daily reversal to illiquidity and documents a sign flip toward momentum for the handful of largest and most tradeable cryptocurrencies.
signal: Prior completed UTC day close-to-close return. Within the most-liquid bucket rank in the momentum direction; within the remaining bucket rank in the reversal direction.
universe: Point-in-time assets with at least 30 days exact hourly history and valid lagged trailing 30-day close*volume; minimum 8 assets.
rebalance: Daily 00:00 UTC at current open using only prior-hour/prior-day data.
construction: Allocate 0.5 gross to the liquid momentum sleeve and 0.5 gross to the less-liquid reversal sleeve. Each sleeve is dollar-neutral: half its gross long and half short, using within-sleeve return halves.
development_gate: Canonical base-cost net Sharpe > 0.70, positive net total return, and at least 2 of 3 preregistered liquidity splits have positive development return.
limitations: The prepared panel contains 19 liquid Binance perpetuals rather than 3600+ spot coins, so the less-liquid sleeve is relative within a liquid-perp universe. Funding is unavailable.
